strings.tutorial.ask.general: Press G for your goals and the next step, or open a panel from the numbered buttons on the left.
strings.tutorial.guided.goals: Press G for your goals and the next step. The card on the right always shows what to do next.
strings.tutorial.guided.tooltip: Every number explains itself. Hover over the 10-year yield in the top bar, or click it to pin the explanation and follow the causes down.
strings.tutorial.guided.unpause: Press Space or a speed button to let time run. The game pauses itself when something needs you.
strings.tutorial.guided.whip: Open 03 Congress. Draft a bill, then ask for a {g:whip_count}: it tells you who is likely to vote yes, and how sure the whips are.
strings.tutorial.guided.xdates: Nobody knows exactly when the money runs out. Open 07 Intel: each estimator publishes an {g:x_date} range, and they differ.
strings.tutorial.hint.approval_slide: Your approval has slid about 5 points in a month. Check Public, and what your advisors are worried about on the Overview.
strings.tutorial.hint.bill_on_desk: A bill you didn't write is on your desk. Sign it, or veto it: Congress can override with two thirds of both chambers.
strings.tutorial.hint.capital_low: You are low on {g:political_capital}. It recovers every day, faster when approval is high; favours and orders spend it.
strings.tutorial.hint.first_court_case: A court case takes weeks. The ruling depends on the law and on the judges, not on your approval.
strings.tutorial.hint.first_crisis: A crisis moves in stages. Each response has a cost; doing nothing is also a choice.
strings.tutorial.hint.first_incident: Something happened along one of your orders' chains: a refusal, a leak, a resignation. Incidents are listed under Orders.
strings.tutorial.hint.first_negotiation: In a negotiation, every offer costs the other side face. Push too hard and they walk away; give too much and your own side notices.
strings.tutorial.hint.first_whip: A whip count is a forecast, not a promise. Paler seats are less certain; members can mislead the whips. Ask again after you change the bill.
strings.tutorial.hint.must_at_risk: A goal you must not fail is at risk. Press G to see which, and what helps.
strings.tutorial.hint.order_moot: One of your orders is no longer needed: what it was for has been settled. It will still be carried out, with its costs, unless you withdraw it on Orders.
strings.tutorial.hint.order_trouble: One of your orders hit resistance. On Orders you can insist in writing, replace those who refused, or withdraw it.
strings.tutorial.hint.panel_cabinet: Cabinet: open a row for an advisor's record and replacements. Follow their advice and their influence grows.
strings.tutorial.hint.panel_congress: Congress: the chambers, your bills and the whip counts. Draft, submit, count, then win the votes you're short.
strings.tutorial.hint.panel_economy: Economy: published statistics are dots (and get revised), market data is a line. Forecast runs six quarters ahead; policies can be enacted or need a bill.
strings.tutorial.hint.panel_factions: Factions: the blocs and groups that move votes and opinion. Their loyalty is hidden; read their signals and spend favours where you need them.
strings.tutorial.hint.panel_intel: Intel: estimates, reports and releases. Each says how reliable it is; a report's confidence can itself be wrong.
strings.tutorial.hint.panel_log: The Log keeps every event and every decision others made, with their reasons. Filter by kind.
strings.tutorial.hint.panel_orders: Orders: pick a field, then an order, and build it with the chips. Counsel judges it before you give it; the people in the chain decide whether it happens.
strings.tutorial.hint.panel_overview: The Overview: indicators with their last 90 days, deadlines and your advisors' concerns. Hover any number for its causes.
strings.tutorial.hint.panel_public: Public: approval is a polling average. Single polls are noisy; voter groups are crosstabs and even noisier.
strings.tutorial.hint.panel_world: World: foreign leaders, how they see you, and talks. Creditors watch the debt limit closely.
strings.tutorial.hint.shutdown: The government is shut down. Funding needs a bill too; a long shutdown costs approval and the economy.
strings.tutorial.hint.xdate_close: The {g:x_date} is less than a month away and the debt limit isn't fixed. Get a bill through, or prepare for what happens if you can't.
strings.tutorial.offer_full: New to the game? The full tutorial walks you through every panel with the clock held.
strings.tutorial.panel.cabinet.1: Open a row for the advisor's record and the candidates who could replace them.
strings.tutorial.panel.cabinet.2: Following an advisor's advice raises their influence; overruling them costs their faction's loyalty.
strings.tutorial.panel.congress.1: Draft a bill, submit it, then ask for a whip count to see who is short.
strings.tutorial.panel.congress.2: The House needs a majority of its members. The Senate needs 60 to end a filibuster.
strings.tutorial.panel.congress.3: Rewrite a bill to win a bloc, but watch for poison pills: provisions another bloc can't accept.
strings.tutorial.panel.economy.1: Dots are published estimates; circles are earlier estimates since revised.
strings.tutorial.panel.economy.2: Forecast runs your economy six quarters ahead on several possible futures: the shaded fan is the range.
strings.tutorial.panel.economy.3: Some policies you can enact yourself; others need a bill in Congress.
strings.tutorial.panel.factions.1: Filter by your party, the other party, or groups outside Congress.
strings.tutorial.panel.factions.2: A bloc's wants and stakes tell you what a bill or a favour needs to offer them.
strings.tutorial.panel.factions.3: Favours cost political capital. The bloc remembers, and so do its rivals.
strings.tutorial.panel.intel.1: The Treasury's X-date range is the most reliable; private analysts guess wider.
strings.tutorial.panel.intel.2: Invest in insight on a leader to learn their red lines and pressures. It costs political capital.
strings.tutorial.panel.intel.3: A report's stated confidence can itself be wrong. Check its reliability.
strings.tutorial.panel.log.1: Filter by kind to find a decision; each one says why it was made.
strings.tutorial.panel.log.2: Click a headline to open the panel it belongs to.
strings.tutorial.panel.orders.1: Pick a field, then an order. Each part of it is a row of chips; countries can be picked on the map.
strings.tutorial.panel.orders.2: Counsel's verdict and your advisors' predictions update as you change the order.
strings.tutorial.panel.orders.3: Extreme orders ask once more before they go. Nothing is blocked: the world answers.
strings.tutorial.panel.overview.1: Hover any number for what moves it; click to pin and follow the causes down.
strings.tutorial.panel.overview.2: Deadlines count down here. The X-date range is the Treasury's latest estimate.
strings.tutorial.panel.overview.3: Advisors' concerns show who is worried about what. The most alarmed are first.
strings.tutorial.panel.public.1: Approval is the polling average; the dots are single polls with their house effects.
strings.tutorial.panel.public.2: The map shows estimated approval by state while this panel is open.
strings.tutorial.panel.public.3: Voter groups past the dashed line approve of you on balance.
strings.tutorial.panel.world.1: Show on map frames a country and opens its dossier.
strings.tutorial.panel.world.2: Relations move with what you do: a default alarms creditors, talks and reassurance help.
strings.tutorial.panel.world.3: Open talks to negotiate a deal; every offer costs the other side face.
strings.tutorial.step.cabinet: Open 08 Cabinet and open an advisor's row: their record, their advice, and who could replace them. Advisors you follow gain influence.
strings.tutorial.step.camera: Move around the map: drag it with the mouse (or use WASD), and zoom with the wheel. Try both.
strings.tutorial.step.congress: Only Congress can raise the debt limit. Open 03 Congress: the House needs a majority (218 when every seat is filled); the Senate needs 60 to end a filibuster ({g:cloture}).
strings.tutorial.step.decision: Decisions come to you as they happen. When one arrives, read what your advisors recommend, then choose. Doing nothing is also a choice: if time runs out, your staff decide.
strings.tutorial.step.done: That's the desk. 10 Log keeps everything that happened and why; save from the menu (Esc). Lost? Click the beacon at the bottom left, or press H, for a hint about whatever is open. Good luck.
strings.tutorial.step.draft: Press Draft a bill. Add a provision that raises or suspends the debt limit, watch the projected votes, and save the draft.
strings.tutorial.step.economy_world: Two more panels: 02 Economy (charts, the forecast, policies) and 06 World (leaders, relations, talks). Open both.
strings.tutorial.step.favour: Short of votes? Open 04 Factions, open a bloc you need, and offer a favour. It costs {g:political_capital}, and they remember who helped them.
strings.tutorial.step.goals: What are you trying to do? Press G (or the Goals button on the right) to see your goals and the next step. The card on the right always shows that next step.
strings.tutorial.step.intel: Nobody knows the X-date exactly. Open 07 Intel: the Treasury, the CBO and private analysts each publish a range, and they disagree because they see different data. Trust the Treasury's most.
strings.tutorial.step.modes: The bar at the bottom of the map switches {g:map_mode}s. Choose Opinion, then click Japan: the dossier shows its leader and how they see you.
strings.tutorial.step.orders: Open 09 Orders. Choose Information, then Run a messaging campaign. Read counsel's verdict and your advisors' predictions, then give the order. Orders pass through people, and people can say no.
strings.tutorial.step.overview: The numbered buttons on the left open your staff's panels. Open 01 Overview: indicators with their last 90 days, deadlines, crises and your advisors' concerns.
strings.tutorial.step.public: Open 05 Public: your {g:approval} as a polling average, and the map turns to estimated approval by state. Click a state to open its dossier.
strings.tutorial.step.time: Now start the clock. Press Space or a speed button (1 to 5); Space pauses again. Whatever you do while paused happens when the next day begins, and the game pauses itself when something needs you. Let three days go by.
strings.tutorial.step.tooltip: Every number explains itself. Click the 10-year yield to pin its explanation, then click one of its causes to follow it down.
strings.tutorial.step.welcome: Welcome to the White House. The map is the country; everything else is your staff, one click away. The clock is held for the first tour: nothing happens until you start it.
strings.tutorial.step.whip: Submit your bill, then ask for a {g:whip_count}: Legislative Affairs counts who will vote yes. Members can mislead the whips, so read the certainty.
strings.tutorial.step.wire: On the right: decisions that need you, then the news wire. Fold the wire away for more map, then bring it back.
strings.tutorial.step.xdate: The bar along the top is your instrument panel. The dates in the middle are the {g:x_date}: when the Treasury runs out of room under the {g:debt_limit}. Hover over them.
strings.tutorial.term.approval.def: The share of voters who approve of you, as a polling average. Marked * because it is an estimate.
strings.tutorial.term.cloture.def: Ending a Senate debate. It takes 60 votes, so a minority can block a bill by filibuster.
strings.tutorial.term.debt_limit.def: The legal cap on federal borrowing. Only Congress can raise or suspend it.
strings.tutorial.term.extraordinary_measures.def: Accounting moves that let the Treasury keep paying for a while after the debt limit is reached.
strings.tutorial.term.map_mode.def: What the map's colours show: approval, delegations, or how foreign leaders see you.
strings.tutorial.term.perceived.def: A number marked * is what was published, not the truth: it can be late or revised.
strings.tutorial.term.political_capital.def: What you spend to get things done: favours, orders, insight. It recovers every day, faster when approval is high.
strings.tutorial.term.technical_default.def: Payments missed for a few days and then made good. Survivable, but it costs.
strings.tutorial.term.whip_count.def: A count of how members say they will vote. Members can mislead the whips.
strings.tutorial.term.x_date.def: The day the Treasury can no longer pay every bill on time without borrowing more. Estimated, never known exactly.
strings.ui.tutorial.menu_note: Learn every part of the game, step by step, with the clock held.
strings.ui.tutorial.paused_note: Your staff act when the next day begins: press Space to let time run.
strings.ui.tutorial.time_locked: The clock is held for the first tour. You'll start it in a few steps, in the chapter about time.
